overall_verdict: Reject a topology-only quantitative edge-stiffness guarantee. The ideal Maxwell/SSH index controls a zero-mode count under its assumptions, but numerical and physical stiffness depend on local energetic terms, supports, prestress, finite size, probes, and boundary realization. A finite-chain perturbation theorem is useful but adjacent to existing results and not claimed novel.

claims.claim: Mechanical SSH winding/polarization gives a boundary zero-mode index for an ideal gapped Maxwell chain under specified unit-cell gauge and termination assumptions.
claims.scope: Index/count result, not a numerical force-displacement stiffness theorem. Bulk gap and boundary/local termination contribution matter.

claims.claim: For C with (Cu)_i=q1*u_i+q2*u_(i+1), q1,q2>0 and unequal, H0=C^T C has a geometric zero mode and ideal bulk gap Delta=(q2-q1)^2. Adding endpoint penalty kappa lifts the mode at first order with coefficient equal to the normalized zero mode endpoint weight rho.
assumptions: N-1 compatibility constraints on N generalized coordinates
unit masses or stated generalized-coordinate norm
only the specified positive-semidefinite endpoint penalty
q1 and q2 positive and unequal
claims.falsifier: In the stated matrix model, lambda1/kappa fails to converge to rho as kappa tends to zero, the ideal nonzero spectrum violates the stated gap, or the lowest mode does not reverse localization when q1 and q2 are exchanged.

claims.claim: Topology alone determines a material-independent quantitative stiffness contrast for a finite physical metamaterial.
claims.argument: A local boundary support term changes the low mode eigenvalue and edge compliance while leaving bulk winding unchanged. Material hinge stiffness, prestress, clamping and finite-size overlap also vary independently of the index.

claims.claim: A small boundary penalty can be certified to preserve a separated soft mode in the specified finite-chain model.
claims.statement: For H_kappa=H0+kappa P with P=e1e1^T+eNeN^T, the minimum eigenvalue is bounded by the Rayleigh penalty of the ideal zero mode; first-order perturbation gives lambda1=kappa rho+O(kappa^2/Delta). Standard eigenspace perturbation controls mode rotation when kappa norm(P) is small relative to the gap.
claims.qualification: Model-level only; calibrated parasitic support stiffness and the measured bulk gap are inputs, not consequences of topology.

claims.claim: The numerical check validates physical fabrication or novelty.
claims.evidence: The check is only dense eigensolves of 40x40 model matrices; it tests a reconstructed algebraic model and does not cover 2D lattices, disorder, dynamics, friction, or experimental fixtures.

bounded_check.result: For N=40, q1=0.4, q2=1.0, Delta=0.36, rho=0.84; at kappa=1e-5 lambda1/kappa=0.8399984, lambda2=0.362466, and ideal-mode overlap is 0.99999999999. Swapping q1,q2 reverses endpoint localization.
bounded_check.cost: One 40x40 dense eigendecomposition per parameter point; no physical data.

costs_and_falsifiers.decisive_measurement: Measure modes/edge compliance with matched fixtures and calibrated hinge/support stiffness; swap dimerization and use an equally informed nonpolarized control. A contrast that does not follow measured Hessian and coupling reversal falsifies the simplified realization model, not the ideal index theorem.
costs_and_falsifiers.costs: Fabrication, geometric metrology, coupon tests, force/displacement calibration, mode scanning, matched fixtures, repeat trials, and uncertainty estimates; monetary costs depend on the fabrication and instrumentation route and were not estimated.

references: Kane and Lubensky, Topological Boundary Modes in Isostatic Lattices, https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0554
Rocks and Mehta, Integrating local energetics into Maxwell-Calladine constraint counting to design mechanical metamaterials, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07419
Xiu et al., Topological transformability and reprogrammability of multistable mechanical metamaterials, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2211725119
